owns.rule: Customer Organization, Contact, Dispatch Location and Local User Profile identities are distinct first-class records with immutable internal identity.
Contact identity is independent from name/email and Customer affiliation; current affiliation is at most one while prior affiliations remain historical evidence.
Shared candidate reconciliation is deterministic, scope-aware and exact; ambiguity is returned rather than guessed.
Shared reference archival/reactivation semantics preserve history and block changes that would strand active dependencies.
Dispatch Location remains customer-neutral and operation-neutral even when linked to one Site or reused by logistics operations.
The shared Settings surface routes typed settings to their semantic owner and HLD-02 persistence without becoming a duplicate source of truth.

shared_with.boundary: HLD-09 owns Site creation/ownership; HLD-03 owns Dispatch Location identity. The application command creates/links both atomically without either module directly mutating the other's private persistence.
HLD-03 owns reusable Contact/channel identity and validity; communications/inventory own when an action requires or snapshots a channel.
HLD-03 owns matching semantics; HLD-05 owns source staging/proposal/review workflow.

does_not_own.capability: authentication secrets, password verifier, auto-login material
Site, Cloud Deployment, Room, Rack, Network Element, Component
Spare Request requester lifecycle and logistics snapshots
Product Line, Contract and Contract Product Line reference semantics

authority_rules: Email is matching/channel data, not a global Contact key.
Customer affiliation change never creates a replacement Contact by default.
Reference matching never silently mutates or merges records.
Archived references remain history-visible but are not eligible for new active relationships until explicit reactivation.
Domain-specific settings remain semantically owned by their domain even when edited from a shared Settings workspace.
